name: Chinese Calligraphy
visualIdentity: Normalized from calligraphic subtitles and seal imagery. Center the design on authentic brush gesture, deliberate character spacing, and negative space. Vertical text, vermilion seals, and limited imagery may support it. Use a consistent script and accurate wording; verify glyphs and stroke order.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to poetry and cultural greetings, especially with restrained ink wash imagery. Its strong focal gestures may also suit explanatory or editorial narratives. That broader suitability is inferred; prioritize calligraphy and meaningful text.
limitations: Use verified glyph paths or authentic calligraphy assets. A font outline cannot stand in for brush strokes: writing animation needs separate stroke paths in correct order. Reveal complete groups or follow real stroke order; never stretch characters. Keep imagery secondary and avoid large wash areas. Chapter effects are optional and should not obscure meaning or break continuous shots or loops.
palette: Suggested new-art palette: paper background #F5EFDE, ink foreground #20211E, and optional vermilion seal #B4382A. These are suggestions, not canonical colors; preserve exact task, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors and their roles. Use discrete tokens with no gradient. Check actual composited text contrast; do not recolor artwork to improve it.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal complete character groups or animate verified strokes in correct order, with reading holds and restrained transitions. Optional ink wash may fade in after calligraphy completes. For interactive HTML, scrolling may control coherent chapter or story states; reversing and direct seeking should restore the same states. Video must use composition time, never live scroll or pointer input.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping or competing vocals, and synchronize picture and sound.
assetRequirements: Prepare authentic calligraphy layers or verified glyph paths; animated writing requires ordered, separate stroke paths. Preserve transparency, consistent dimensions, and clear filenames. Verify exact wording, script, glyphs, and stroke order. Inspect assets before composition; preserve asset colors.
combinations: Usually strongest alone. Suggested pairing: style-038 ink wash as limited secondary imagery for poetry or cultural greetings; calligraphy stays dominant, black and vermilion only, with verified stroke order. Wash fades in after calligraphy completes; avoid large wash areas and outlined-font strokes.
productionApproach: Choose SVG for scalable glyph paths and masks, with GSAP DrawSVGPlugin for controlled stroke reveals when needed. HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation prevents a required output, and record why. Keep visual construction and motion design in their own layers, use deterministic seekable time for video, and inspect rendered frames, full video, text, audio sync, and delivery settings. Interactive scroll controls belong only in HTML delivery.
